summary: Willamette NF L-4 cab on Carpenter Mountain; NHLR says CCC built it in 1935, USFS says 1934; staffed in fire season; one-mile trail; NHLR US 484.

access.note: Reached by a one-mile trail from the Carpenter Mountain Trailhead on Forest Road 350; the Forest Service says it is not available for public rental

visit.trail_note: About 1.0 mile on Carpenter Mountain Trail 3302, rated moderate, from the trailhead on Forest Road 350

events.note: Government lookout on the summit found a fire ten miles northeast of Belknap Springs
Early structure: NHLR calls it an open-sided fire shelter; Forest Lookouts calls it a cupola-style house
Lookout spotted a fire about a quarter-mile wide near the county's southern boundary
Lightning struck the telephone wire to the lookout station
Current L-4 cab built by the CCC per NHLR; Forest Service dates it to 1934
Alvin Blankenship was the fireman for the season; a 1939 newspaper item said a lookout was most important on this peak
Lightning damage: 14 windows blown out, roof lifted off its frame; under repair afterward
Forest Service lists a 1995 renovation; Firelookout says restored in the 1990s

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The NHLR and Forest Lookouts (1935) and Firelookout (1935) disagree with the Forest Service (1934). The story gives both dates and attributes each.

The NHLR calls the 1917 structure an open-sided fire shelter. The Forest Lookouts page calls it a cupola-style house. Firelookout describes a rag camp and open shelter, and a government lookout was already reporting fires in 1914. The story notes the differences.
The NHLR gives 5,190 ft (1,582 m), which matches the record's 1,581.9 m. The Forest Service gives 5,349 ft and Firelookout and Cherylhill give 5,369 ft. The record was left unchanged.

notes_for_editor: The record's ground kind is supported by Cherylhill's L-4 Ground Cabin, though the NHLR's with-catwalk wording suggests a raised cab; the record was left as it was. Build year and elevation conflicts are reported in the story and resolved_conflicts. The Forest Service page is the current source for staffing and rental status. No photos added.
